title: Render Contract — the JSON handover from the script pipeline to video_generation
description: The canonical machine handover: projects/structured_scripts/<name>.json. Produced by render-contract-compiler (stage 24), validated by contract-linter (stage 25), consumed by storyboard/source_parser.py (parse() branches on the .json extension and maps this 1:1 onto SourceScript/Scene/AnimationBullet — everything downstream of the parser is unchanged). Carries the S7 master-clock enrichments (sentence durations, pauses, emphasis, roles) that the legacy .txt flattened into comments.

script_ready.description: The literal SCRIPT-READY line (render_gate.sh greps this raw text). Pending: 'SCRIPT-READY: REQUIRED — Phase-1 gates not yet passed'. Evidenced: 'SCRIPT-READY: <name> | sync=<NN>/100 wonder=<N>/10 gates=...'.

global_style.description: GLOBAL VISUAL STYLE block (LOOK · RENDER STYLE · TEXTURE · SHAPE · GRID+SPACING · TYPE · PALETTE · LIGHTING · THROUGH-LINE · HOMES of recurring elements) — denormalized onto every scene by the parser.

reference_assets.description: REFERENCE ASSETS manifest — real screenshots to place in public/img/.

concepts.description: THE CONCEPT SPINE (provenance thread): the cognitive model's concept list exported top-level — the ground truth of what the video must teach. Every beat's semantics.concept references one of these ids; contract_scorecard.py counts CONCEPT COVERAGE (every concept visibly taught by >=1 beat; every beat traces to a concept). Producer: render-contract-compiler (from cognitive-model-engine); consumers: the scorecard + beats + S5 sentence concept_tags (same id space).

id.description: stable concept id (the same ids S5 sentences carry as concept_tag)

shape.description: the cognitive shape (comparison | decomposition | flow | hierarchy | timeline | cause-effect | part-to-whole | transformation)

misconception.description: the belief this concept's beat(s) must visibly replace

numbers_ledger.description: The video's quantified WORLD (from research-engine's knowledge package): every quantity that may appear on any instrument/panel/HUD/chart/derivation, plus derived values — all mutually consistent. The render may only display ledger (or narration) values; it never invents numbers. A thin ledger starves instruments — carry MORE real numbers, not fewer.

expr.description: The arithmetic over quantity ids (e.g. 'n01 / n02') — shown on screen when the beat derives it.

series.description: RENDER-SHAPED data (the anti-text-slide deliverable): real multi-point data — samples over time, a distribution, per-item rows — that charts/instruments animate from. A scalar supports only a reading; an animated chart/curve/row-fill REQUIRES a series. Every planned chart in the scenes must trace to one of these.

points.description: the real data points, from the source

trace.description: The running example EXECUTED step-by-step through the mechanism — real intermediate values per pass, so a scene's `cycle` replays a genuine computation instead of a decorative loop.

consistency.description: Statement that every derived value was recomputed and any two on-screen appearances of one quantity agree.

clock.description: S7 verification-pass lock metadata (the master clock).

description.description: SCENE DESCRIPTION prose brief (Environment · Situation · Realization · Emotional Journey · Visual Transformation · Final Image).

design.description: SCENE DESIGN field block (LOCATION · CAST · PRIMARY FOCUS · ATTENTION FLOW · CINEMATIC · THROUGH-LINE STATE · ...).

cast.description: THE TYPED CAST — the scene's world as DATA, not prose (the object graph from visual-world-engine/object-library-engine, carried through the seam so the renderer never re-interprets English). Every scene needs ≥1 object with kind='world-object' (a physical thing — machine/page/vessel/figure — never a text panel). Ops' obj/to fields and on-screen labels resolve against these ids.

id.description: stable id ops and labels reference (e.g. 'page', 'shredder')

kind.description: world-object = physical thing with form; instrument = a gauge/meter/card DISPLAYING values; label = text welded to an owner

form.description: the concrete physical form, drawable without interpretation (e.g. 'dark machine block with intake slot and teeth')

material.description: paper | glass | metal | glow | ink — picks easing + light behaviour

accent.description: the entity's locked color token name (e.g. 'red')

home.description: its fixed screen region (from the world model's HOMES)

states.description: its lifecycle states used in this scene (from the object library)

owner.description: for kind=label/instrument: the cast id it is welded to / reports on — REQUIRED for labels (the referent gate)

stage.description: SCENE-DRIVEN architecture: the scene's PERSISTENT WORLD — the one settled composite (zones + cast at their homes + atmosphere) plus the scene's RUNNING MECHANISMS, alive for the scene's WHOLE duration on scene-local time (mechanism cycles never reset at beat boundaries). The renderer draws the stage continuously; bullets are MODULATIONS of it (spotlight a station, change a rate, land a payoff), never re-declarations of the world. A scene without `stage` falls back to self-contained beats (legacy).

composite.description: the settled FINAL-FRAME layout as one spec: every element of every beat placed together in disjoint reserved zones (overlap impossible by reservation) — beats progressively reveal/modulate this one composite. INCLUDES CORRIDORS: every mover's swept path (a sweep/travel/dock/cycle circuit) is reserved like a zone — a corridor crosses no text zone and no occupied zone, because transform-animated elements overlay whatever they cross (the renderer never reflows for motion).

zones.description: THE MACHINE-CHECKABLE geometry of the composite (the script-side overlap gate): every reserved region as a fractional rect. contract-linter verifies mechanically (scripts/composite_lint.py): element/text zones pairwise DISJOINT; corridors cross no text/element zone; every cast home resolves to a zone. Overlap is prevented AT THE SCRIPT, before any render exists.

kind.description: element = an object's home; text = a label/reading region; corridor = a mover's swept path (may cross nothing occupied)

region.description: [x, y, w, h] as fractions of canvas (0..1)

occupant.description: the cast id (or mover id) reserved into this zone

process.description: mechanisms that run for the ENTIRE scene (same shape as semantics.process): the machine keeps operating while beats come and go — the reference-grade continuous world.

object.description: a cast id — the thing that cycles

circuit.description: ordered station refs (cast ids / regions) traversed each pass

emits.description: what each pass visibly produces and where it lands (a reading on a cast id)

rate.description: the narrated per-unit meaning of one pass

camera.description: THE CAMERA TRACK (from camera-director, stage 14) — exported so it reaches the renderer instead of dying in-memory. The camera carries MEANING; without this field the render is camera-locked (a flat-render failure class). Realized deterministically (push = scale the focal group up; pull = scale down to reveal scale; parallax = layers at different rates).

move.description: push | pull | orbit | pan | tilt | rack | whip | macro | parallax | locked

target.description: a cast id — what the move frames/points at (default = the beat's payoff / the through-line)

meaning.description: why this move (importance = push · scale = pull · depth = parallax · unease = tilt · discovery = orbit)

shot.description: wide | medium | close | extreme-close (the dominant framing; per-beat changes ride the bullet's shot/visual_intent)

headline.description: ≤8-word beat identity — MACHINE METADATA ONLY (logs/QA/cache keys); prefix '[REPLACE] ' for a full-backdrop replace beat. NEVER rendered as on-screen text: this field is not part of the frame. The ONLY source of on-screen words is the opt-in `text` field (and readings on instruments). Rendering the headline was the structural per-beat text quota that produced text-rich output.

narration.description: THIS beat's spoken sentences, in order (pair-block coupling — the anchor comes from these). The parser joins them (adding <pause Xs> from pause_after_ms) into the scene narration for TTS/Whisper.

id.description: S7 sentence id (e.g. s014) — the master-clock binding.

text.description: Spoken text; numbers as words; may embed <pause Xs> tags directly.

emphasis_word.description: At most one — what the voice stresses and the visuals Emphasize.

what_happens.description: Human-readable ILLUSTRATION of the beat (prose for reviewers). Where a `semantics` block exists it is AUTHORITATIVE and this prose only illustrates it — the renderer builds from semantics, never re-interprets this text.

semantics.description: THE AUTHORITATIVE beat spec — world physics, not storyboard verbs (what must BECOME TRUE, not how to tween it). Exported from the state/event graphs (stages 9-11) so they reach the renderer instead of dying in-memory. Realization is compiled deterministically from the video's style-locked verb→topology table — never re-chosen per render (determinism + film consistency).

concept.description: the concept id (from top-level `concepts`) this beat teaches — the provenance thread from cognitive model → beat → proof. The scorecard counts coverage both ways.

transitions.description: Object state deltas: cast id + lifecycle state from → to (the state graph's diff).

relationships.description: First-class RELATIONSHIP deltas — edges between cast ids whose strength changes (e.g. adjacency(label,value) 1.0 → 0.0). The relationship, not an object, is the subject.

invariants.description: What the beat must PRESERVE and what it deliberately BREAKS — the teaching stated as constraints.

process.description: RUNNING MECHANISMS sustained through the beat (Run events / the state's `process` field): a subject repeatedly traverses a circuit, each pass visibly emitting an effect. The renderer realizes each as a `cycle` — the beat's honest hold-alive. Required whenever the beat's narration describes per-unit/rate/repeated behavior.

object.description: a cast id — the thing that cycles

circuit.description: ordered station refs (cast ids / regions) traversed each pass

emits.description: what each pass visibly produces and where it lands (a reading on a cast id)

rate.description: the narrated per-unit meaning of one pass

proof.description: The beat's checkable outcome: what the viewer should realize + a MEASURABLE visual predicate the proof gate verifies on rendered frames (geometry: distances, counts, luminance — mechanically checkable).

predicate.description: e.g. 'distance(maxLabel, price200) increases monotonically across the beat'

attention.description: THE EYE PATH for this beat (from attention-director, stage 13) — exported so the renderer directs the eye deterministically instead of the author guessing. SERIAL ATTENTION: one focus at a time; everything not in focus dims/settles.

focus.description: a cast id — the ONE element the eye lands on this beat (the kinetic focus)

order.description: cast ids in the order the eye visits them across the beat (the path)

dim.description: cast ids pushed to the periphery this beat (spotlight-dim; the two-tier texture class)

transition.description: THE BOUNDARY HANDOFF into this beat (from transition-designer, stage 20) — exported as TYPED data (was prose in `design`). Rendering-library-independent: it declares WHAT happens at the cut, not how React does it. The declared `carry` is what runtime telemetry then verifies — R7 (single instance, no ghost) + R5 (the carried element holds its HOME across the cut).

mode.description: evolve (settled priors + delta — the default) | replace (composite-out → skeleton-in → data-in) | match-cut | morph | dock | fade-through | hard-cut

carry.description: the cast id carried ACROSS this boundary as a SINGLE instance (match-cut/morph/dock/persistent) — the shared-element that must not be double-drawn; null for a clean evolve/replace

text.description: OPT-IN on-screen label — ≤3 words or one number, ONLY when the frame fails the deaf-viewer test without it (scene-composer's label budget: ≈ one headline + a few labels per SCENE, not per beat). Empty string / omitted = no new label, the world carries the beat. A term's first appearance requires its owner object on stage (cast owner — linter Check 3d).

visual_intent.description: One-phrase hint for the choreographer (from S5) — never a storyboard.

audio_anchor.description: 2–4 word phrase VERBATIM from this bullet's own narration sentences (parser enforces).

ops.description: Optional compiled motion operators (one per beat event): {op, obj, to, token, choreo, sync} — op from the closed set. Null → the motion compiler infers from what_happens.

motion.description: THE MOTION SCORE (stages 14/16/17 exported as INTENT) — how the beat's world BEHAVES, so the codegen builds cinematic motion instead of inventing generic tweens. Carries the choreography + physics FEEL; the exact easing/duration/springs resolve at Phase-2 via the style-locked (action,intensity)->(easing,duration) table — never baked per beat (the semantics<->timing boundary). Disciplined by serial attention: rich on the hero/impact beat, restrained on support. A motion score left as free-form prose is a determinism smell; the score steps are STRUCTURED tokens.

operator.description: the closed-set operator(s) realizing the beat (e.g. 'dock + count(overshoot)')

material.description: metal | ink | glow | paper | glass — picks the physics character

intensity.description: serial-attention tier — only hero/impact beats get camera + particulate reaction

score.description: the ordered micro-beats (anticipation -> action -> secondary -> settle) as STRUCTURED, machine-parseable steps — never free-form prose.

actor.description: the thing that moves — a cast id or a named sub-part (e.g. 'stamp_arm')

action.description: a verb from the CLOSED operator set (slam|dock|count|split|ignite|flash|shake|travel|snap|...) — the closed vocabulary is what makes realization deterministic and film-consistent

intensity.description: anticipation | hard | medium | soft — resolves to (easing, duration) via the Phase-2 style table

target.description: optional — the cast id / value the action lands on

secondary.description: restrained supporting motion (the running mechanism + particulate on hero beats), same step shape

camera_reaction.description: the camera's beat-level reaction (punch-in on impact, etc.) — 'none' on restrained beats

light_reaction.description: the lighting reaction (a flash/bloom on impact) — 'steady' on restrained beats

physics_feel.description: the FEEL (anticipation/overshoot/follow-through) — intent, never spring constants

realization_note.description: how (action, intensity) resolve to (easing, duration) at Phase-2

constraints.description: RENDER CONSTRAINTS exported from the Capability Registry — binding on ANY renderer consuming this contract (ours or external). Violating a constraint = non-conformant render. Emitted by render-contract-compiler.

audio.description: The AUDIO TRACK (stage 19 audio-design-engine output). Narration synthesis + mux is MANDATORY — a silent render is non-conformant.

voice.description: engine + loudness target (e.g. piper, -14 LUFS integrated, TP<-1.5)

music.description: bed arc per scene + duck_db under voice + asset status (wired|GAP)

sfx.description: cues: {scene, beat, on (anchor/event), sound, asset: wired|GAP}

silences.description: designed drops (scene, after-sentence id, bed-cut true/false)
